categories.label: Categories
categories.description: Manage the categories used to classify transactions.
categories.pageDescription: System categories are shared and cannot be edited. Ones you create can be renamed, reordered, deactivated, or deleted once no longer in use.

transactionTypes.label: Transaction types
transactionTypes.description: Map the raw labels from your bank statement to Lumio's transaction types.
transactionTypes.pageDescription: For each raw label used by your bank statement (e.g. "Transfer"), choose here which type Lumio should treat it as. The change also applies to already-imported transactions — except the ones you've already corrected by hand, which stay untouched.

noParsers.title: No labels yet
noParsers.description: This page fills up after your first PDF bank statement import (e.g. Trade Republic).

noLabels.title: No labels observed
noLabels.description: No transaction imported with this parser carries a raw label yet.

page.reappliedWithSkipped_one: {{count}} transaction updated, {{skipped}} left untouched because edited by hand.
page.reappliedWithSkipped_other: {{count}} transactions updated, {{skipped}} left untouched because edited by hand.

page.infoButton: What does changing the currency mean?

baseCurrency.label: Reference currency
baseCurrency.description: Used to add up net worth, portfolio, and income/expenses when accounts or investments are in different currencies. It doesn't change the original data, only how it is aggregated.

info.title: What changes
info.aggregated: The reference currency decides which currency is used to add up totals that mix accounts/assets in different currencies — net worth, portfolio value, overall income/expenses.
info.originalPreserved: Every transaction, account, and position ALWAYS keeps its own original currency: changing this setting touches no historical data, only how aggregated totals are computed from now on.
info.missingRate: If an exchange rate is missing for a currency in use, that part stays out of the total but is flagged — never a silent exclusion.

rules.label: Rules
rules.description: Automatically classify transactions based on criteria you define.

ai.label: AI
ai.description: Configure an optional AI provider for automatic classification.
ai.pageDescription: AI is optional: transactions are still classified by rules even without an active profile. You can save multiple profiles (even for the same provider) and activate one at a time.

empty.title: No AI profile

marketData.label: Market data
marketData.description: Configure the quote provider used to refresh investment prices.

page.intro: Market data is optional: without an active provider, positions stay valued at historical cost, with no errors. You can save multiple profiles and activate one at a time.

empty.title: No market data profile
empty.description: Create a profile to value your positions at market price instead of historical cost.

refresh.title: Price refresh
refresh.description: Happens automatically every night. You can also start it right away.

page.noActiveProfile: No active profile: valued at historical cost.

deleteDialog.title: Delete this profile?
deleteDialog.activeWarning: This is the active profile: market data will be disabled after deletion.

providerDescriptions.manual: No automatic refresh: you update each asset's price yourself whenever you want.
providerDescriptions.stooq: Currently unreachable: Stooq introduced an anti-bot protection that blocks automated requests. The code stays ready for when (or if) it becomes reachable again.
providerDescriptions.yahoo: Automatic daily refresh via an unofficial endpoint — best-effort, may stop working without notice. Verified working.
providerDescriptions.custom: You configure the endpoint (e.g. Alpha Vantage, Twelve Data, Finnhub) and the API key: no service is integrated by default.

integrations.label: Integrations
integrations.description: Export your financial data to Google Sheets.
integrations.pageDescription: Google Sheets is an optional integration: it exports your financial data to a Google spreadsheet, refreshable on demand. Disabling it has no effect on the rest of Lumio.

jobs.label: System jobs
jobs.description: Configure automatic jobs and the ones triggered by your actions.

scheduled.title: Scheduled jobs
scheduled.description: They run automatically, with no action needed.

triggered.title: Action-triggered jobs
triggered.description: They only start when you import a file, activate an AI profile, or launch an export.

info.title: Two categories of job
info.scheduled: Scheduled jobs run on their own at fixed intervals (a cron), no matter what you do in the app — which is why they have a real on/off switch here. Turning one off only stops the automatic run: wherever an equivalent manual button exists (e.g. "Refresh now"), that one always stays available.
info.triggered: Action-triggered jobs only start when you (or another workspace user) do something — import a file, activate an AI profile, launch an export. They have no system switch here: you enable or disable them where you already configure them (the workspace AI profile, the Google integration). Here you only see their operational parameters.
info.lock: The padlock on a parameter (including the frequency of scheduled jobs) means the value can't be changed from here: it's fixed in the worker's code and changing it takes more than a simple save.
